summary: Today’s pulse tracks The government can't revive Hearn's Reflecting Pool vandalism charges, a judge rules, Trump doesn’t rule out sending ICE to polling sites; US supreme court to review policy to detain immigrants challenging deportation – live, and Fires break out at French schools as students protest nationwide. Across NPR, Guardian, and BBC, the strongest repeated signals are government, challenging, and charges. In the background, Netanyahu says Flydubai attacker had 'Islamist radical indoctrination' and Putin warns West that Russia is ready to use every weapon to protect Kaliningrad keep the wider picture in motion.

headlines.title: The government can't revive Hearn's Reflecting Pool vandalism charges, a judge rules
headlines.description: Citing "exceptional circumstances," a D.C. judge has ruled that the federal government cannot refile its Reflecting Pool charges against David Hearn, despite pressure from President Trump to do so.

headlines.title: Trump doesn’t rule out sending ICE to polling sites; US supreme court to review policy to detain immigrants challenging deportation – live
headlines.description: Justices will consider whether immigrants have a right to a hearing to determine if they should remain detained while challenging their possible deportation The outlet was scheduled to be a part of the group of media traveling to Texas and Oklahoma with the president today, but was removed from list of newsrooms in place for the trip, per the White House schedule.

headlines.description: The French government holds a crisis meeting as demonstrations grow and become violent in places.

headlines.title: Netanyahu says Flydubai attacker had 'Islamist radical indoctrination'
headlines.description: Israel's prime minister says the pilot who tried to take over the Flydubai plane clearly intended to "down the plane".

headlines.title: Putin warns West that Russia is ready to use every weapon to protect Kaliningrad
headlines.description: Vladimir Putin insists Moscow is "not threatening anyone" and merely responding to statements by Western leaders.

headlines.title: ‘Total class act’: Marie-France van Heel is poised to be a very different PM’s wife
headlines.description: The former marketing executive is expected to play a big role in promoting the UK and could be the most influential spouse in No 10 in years Sarah Brown called Gordon her hero , Samantha Cameron insisted David was “incredibly funny” , while Akshata Murty said Rishi was her best friend . When Marie-France van Heel spoke about her husband, Andy Burnham, in a rare public interview a decade ago, she joked that she had noticed his “good looks … and monobrow”. The spousal humanising of a party leader is a well-worn political tool, but van Heel is likely to be a very different prime ministerial partner. The former senior marketing executive is poised to play a more significant role in promoting Britain than any other spouse in the last two decades, stepping up her political engagements after stepping back from her own corporate career.

headlinePool.title: US borrowing costs hit 24-year high as global bond sell-off intensifies
headlinePool.description: Fears that US deficit is unsustainable also drive UK 30-year bond yields briefly above 6% for first time since 1998 Business live – latest updates The global bond sell-off intensified on Thursday, driving 10-year US government borrowing costs to their highest level in 24 years in a frantic day’s trading. The threat of a renewed round of inflation from the persistently high cost of oil has spooked investors on both sides of the Atlantic, with central banks expected to raise interest rates in the coming months to prevent price increases from becoming embedded.

headlinePool.title: France school protests escalate into ‘urban violence’ as PM calls crisis cabinet meeting
headlinePool.description: About 900 demonstrations, blockades and related incidents under way outside high schools around the country A fast-growing protest by high-school students over long hours, teacher shortages and decaying facilities has escalated into “urban violence”, the French government has warned, as it said many schools would switch to online classes to protect teachers and pupils. The prime minister, Sébastien Lecornu, called a crisis cabinet meeting on Thursday and told ministers to cancel travel plans to deal with the demonstrations, which erupted in the Paris region last week but have snowballed across the country.

headlinePool.title: Conrad ‘Cronos’ Lant, frontman of UK heavy metal band Venom, dies aged 63
headlinePool.description: Singer and bassist helped turn Newcastle band into hugely influential force on thrash and black metal subgenres Conrad Lant, the British heavy metal musician who fronted Venom and ensured the Newcastle band became a huge influence on the genre, has died aged 63. “For more than four decades, Conrad’s voice, bass and vision were at the heart of Venom,” reads a statement from the band. “He created something that changed heavy music for ever. Venom never followed the rules. They forged their own path. And Conrad was there at the centre of it all – uncompromising, fearless and unmistakable.” No cause of death was given.

headlinePool.title: NAZA film-makers say they spoke to more than 100 sources about Israeli actions in Gaza
headlinePool.description: Team behind documentary push back against IDF attempt to discredit its exposure of military systems The team behind the award-winning film NAZA, which details the Israeli military’s targeting policies in Gaza and its alleged acceptance of high numbers of civilian deaths, have revealed they spoke to more than 100 sources with knowledge of the military systems used in the war. The disclosure came in response to an Israel Defense Forces statement seeking to discredit the documentary.

headlinePool.title: Renee Good: Family of US woman killed by ICE agent sues Trump officials
headlinePool.description: Lawyers for Good's family say US officials created "an unprecedented environment for state sponsored violence" in Minneapolis.

headlinePool.title: What happened in the failed execution of Christa Pike - and what next?
headlinePool.description: The convicted killer is in hospital in Tennessee after surviving two lethal injections, in a case that has raised many questions.

headlinePool.title: Hegseth puts the future of warfare in the hands of major Maga donors
headlinePool.description: Installing tech billionaires Elon Musk and Palmer Luckey to Pentagon defense board raises conflict of interest concerns By installing the tech billionaires Elon Musk and Palmer Luckey to advisory roles in a Pentagon project about the future of warfare, the defense secretary, Pete Hegseth, bestowed extraordinary influence on two of Maga’s most significant campaign donors – and both men own companies that benefit from federal defense contracting. The new project, which Hegseth dubbed “Project Meridian” in an event in Quantico, Virginia, on Wednesday, will be led by Pentagon official Emil Michael, a former Uber executive. As the Guardian has reported, Michael made millions in profits off non-public Musk company AI stock while in federal office – and while guiding the Department of Defense’s artificial intelligence efforts.

headlinePool.title: Tennessee governor suspends executions after ‘deeply disturbing’ failed lethal injection
headlinePool.description: Independent inquiry ordered after halted execution of Christa Pike, who was convicted of murder Christa Pike: what we know so far about Tennessee woman’s failed execution Tennessee ’s governor on Thursday said it was “deeply disturbing” that his state botched the execution of a death row prisoner who remained alive and snoring 40 minutes after receiving a double dose of the lethal drug that should have quickly killed her. Bill Lee, a Republican, has suspended all executions in the state until at least the end of the year and ordered an independent inquiry after Wednesday night’s failed attempt to put to death Christa Pike, who was convicted of murder, at the execution chamber in Nashville.

headlinePool.title: UK-Iran national arrested under Terrorism Act over RAF Fairford incident
headlinePool.description: Counter-terrorism police arrest 27-year-old in Westminster, while second man questioned under caution Detectives have arrested a dual UK-Iranian national on suspicion of terrorism offences as part of an investigation into a suspected plot near RAF Fairford. Counter-terrorism police said the 27-year-old man was arrested on Thursday in Westminster on suspicion of preparing terrorist acts under section 5 of the Terrorism Act 2006.
